transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I suppose I'm here because my mind just won't hold onto things anymore. I sit down to write a simple note for this youth maker program I'm involved with... something I could do in my sleep before. But lately... the numbers and words just scatter on me. So... here I am.
When did you first notice your mind couldn't hold onto things like it used to?
About... three weeks ago, I guess. It started right around the time my older sister passed away.
Do you have trouble remembering things that happened before your sister passed away?
No... no, not really. Things before that are... they're fine, mostly. It's just... the recent things.
Do you ever feel confused about where you are or what's going on around you?
No... I don't think so. I know where I am. It's nothing like that.
Do you find it hard to express your thoughts or put your thoughts in order when talking to someone?
No... not really. I mean, the words are there. I just... I don't really talk to many people lately anyway.
Have you been having trouble learning new things since your sister passed away?
I don't know. I haven't... I haven't really tried to learn anything new lately. There hasn't been much of a reason to.
Do you have trouble focusing or paying attention to things?

I suppose... yeah. That's actually part of why I came in. My mind just... it won't hold onto things anymore. I tried to sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program... something I could do in my sleep before. But... the numbers and words just scatter on me. I can't keep them straight.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed since your sister passed away?

I suppose so... yes. Most days... I wake up and there's just this heavy, hollow feeling sitting right in my chest. It doesn't really go away. Even when my wife is trying to talk to me, being kind... I just feel like I'm sitting at the bottom of a well.
Do you find your thoughts are disconnected or don't make sense to you or others?
No, I... I don't think so. My thoughts make sense to me. They're just... hard to hold onto, like I said. But they aren't disconnected.
Do you have trouble staying on topic when speaking?
No, I... I don't think I do. I mean, I know what we're talking about. I just... I don't talk very much these days anyway, so... no.
Do you ever find yourself having trouble finding the right words when trying to explain something?
No... not really. I mean, I know what I want to say. I just... don't have much to say.
Do you find that others have difficulty understanding what you're trying to communicate?
No... I don't think so. When I do speak, they understand me fine. I just... keep to myself mostly, so it doesn't really come up.
Have you noticed any changes in your physical health or experienced any unusual physical symptoms since your sister passed away?
No... I don't think so. I haven't really been paying much attention to it, to be honest. But... no, nothing unusual.
Do you ever find it hard to organize your thoughts in your mind?

I suppose... yeah. It's just... my mind won't really hold onto things anymore. I sat down the other day to write a simple note for this youth maker program... something I used to do in my sleep. But... the numbers and words just sort of scatter on me now.
Did your trouble with holding onto things in your mind start immediately after your sister passed away or was it a few days later?
I suppose it was... right away. It's been about three weeks now... ever since she died.
Do you think your trouble with remembering things is directly related to your sister's passing?
I don't know. I suppose... maybe. I haven't really thought about it like that... I just know it's happening.
Do you find that your memory problems get worse when you're thinking about your sister or feeling sad?
I don't really know... I haven't noticed if it changes. It's just... always kind of a fog lately. I try not to dwell on things.
Do you think your memory problems are worse when you're under stress or pressure to remember something?
I couldn't really say. I don't have a lot of... pressure on me right now. I just stay home, mostly. It's just difficult all the time.
Do you notice your memory getting worse when you're feeling particularly sad about your sister's passing?
I don't... I think I just said, I don't really know. I don't pay attention to exactly when it gets worse. It's just... always bad.
Have your memory problems stayed the same since they started three weeks ago?
I suppose so. It's... it's been about three weeks now. Just... ever since my older sister died, it's been like this. It hasn't really changed.
